page: Google Cloud Platform a4-highgpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized instance within the GPU Machines family. The system incorporates 8 NVIDIA B200 GPUs based on the Blackwell architecture, supplying a total of 1440 GB of GPU video memory. Host processing is delivered by 224 dedicated vCPUs built on x86_64 architecture, paired with 3968.0 GB of system RAM, which provides a high ratio of 17.71 GB of memory per core.

Local host storage is bundled directly with 12885 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity, minimizing latency when loading large datasets into system memory and accelerator memory. Network connectivity does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. While synthetic and application benchmark metrics are not recorded for this profile, the pairing of 224 dedicated threads and extensive host memory prevents bottlenecks during large parallel execution pipelines.

By combining extreme accelerator density, large system RAM, and multi-terabyte local NVMe SSD storage into a single server, the instance delivers high resource efficiency for unified multi-GPU workloads. The platform is engineered specifically for large language model pre-training, distributed deep learning, multi-billion parameter inference, and data-intensive high-performance computing simulations.
